column1: # The REAL-LOST arbitrations: one row per (isa, name, direction) class the
# setjoin reports "the Capstone arm named REG_X on N encodings and QEMU did
# not".  That is a count.  R12.1 forbids BOTH errors it invites -- treating
# the count as a defect list, and quoting a zero obtained by discounting --
# so every class here carries a written decision about what the ENCODING
# does, and setjoin --require-ruled fails if a surviving class has no row.
#   isa       the ISA the class was measured on
#   name      the generic register name the Capstone arm named
#   dir       r | w -- the direction; the two halves of one register can and
#             do go different ways (mipsel's FP condition codes are the
#             worked example: the READ is the container question, the WRITE
#   verdict   QEMU      the encoding does not do it; the incumbent is wrong
#             REAL      the encoding does do it and QEMU must state it
#             CAPSTONE  kept for symmetry; no row uses it yet
#             COVERAGE-PATH  the remedy is named in the reason and NOT done
#   third     what a THIRD decoder says, measured per class by
#             LLVM-SILENT / UNMAPPED.  Two decoders disagreeing settles
#             nothing; this column is what makes the third reading part of
#             the record rather than part of the argument.
# WHAT IS PER-CLASS AND WHAT IS SHARED.  The verdict and the third column are
# each class's OWN measurement -- its own sample, its own witnesses.  The
# REASON is shared where the merits genuinely are one argument across several
# register names: "the vector operand list" is one fact about QEMU's gvec
# expanders whether the operand is xmm3 or v21.  A class with no row here is
# UNRULED and setjoin says so; it does not inherit a verdict from a read one.

column7: div/idiv leave the arithmetic flags architecturally UNDEFINED, which a dependency model must see as a CLOBBER, and the string instructions read DF. QEMU's lazy-flag model leaves cc_op untouched on these paths, so a later flags reader is given a RAW edge to the producer BEFORE the div instead of to the div. The third reading is split, and that split is reported rather than resolved

a rel8/rel32 branch forms its target at decode from its own address and its displacement, and the wire carries that target as the block's branch-target field; naming RIP a SOURCE puts a RAW edge on every branch against a register no instruction in the window writes. LLVM does not name it either, so the incumbent stands alone
retq in 64-bit mode pops through a flat stack segment; SS is not consulted for the address and holds no value the return consumes. LLVM does not name it either
leave OVERWRITES RSP from RBP before the pop, so RSP is a destination and not a source; the value it held is discarded unread. LLVM does not name it either
